question.text: What does safe driving depend on, and how does the manual describe driving?

answer.text: Safe driving depends on good health and making correct decisions, and the manual calls driving one of the riskiest activities you may choose.

teaching.text: Being fit to drive starts with good health and sound decisions, because the manual counts driving among the riskiest things you may choose to do. Remember: Health plus good choices.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safe driving depends on good health and making correct decisions, and the manual calls driving one of the riskiest activities you may choose.

question.text: Why does clear vision matter, and what does the manual advise?

answer.text: Without clear vision you struggle to identify traffic and road conditions, spot trouble and respond in time, so regular eye checks by a licensed eye care professional are advised.

teaching.text: Your eyes find the traffic, the road conditions and the trouble ahead, so a licensed eye care professional should check them regularly. Remember: See clearly, check regularly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without clear vision you struggle to identify traffic and road conditions, spot trouble and respond in time, so regular eye checks by a licensed eye care professional are advised.

question.text: What should you do with required corrective lenses, and what lenses should you avoid at night?

answer.text: If corrective lenses are required, always wear them when driving and avoid dark or tinted lenses at night, because they cut the light you need to see.

teaching.text: If you need corrective lenses, wear them every time you drive, and leave dark or tinted lenses off at night when light is already scarce. Remember: No tint after dark.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If corrective lenses are required, always wear them when driving and avoid dark or tinted lenses at night, because they cut the light you need to see.

question.text: What must drivers who use bioptic telescopic lenses send each year?

answer.text: Drivers who use bioptic telescopic lenses must send the Low Vision Acuity Screening form four hundred twelve-LV to the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit every year.

teaching.text: Drivers with bioptic telescopic lenses send the low vision screening form to the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit once every year. Remember: Bioptic users file yearly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers who use bioptic telescopic lenses must send the Low Vision Acuity Screening form four hundred twelve-LV to the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit every year.

question.text: How often do bioptic lens users file their low vision screening form, and with whom?

answer.text: Bioptic telescopic lens users file the Low Vision Acuity Screening, form four hundred twelve-LV, with the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit every year, so their screening is an annual filing.

teaching.text: For bioptic lens users, screening is an annual filing with the Driver Improvement unit, not something that waits for renewal. Remember: Annual filing, Driver Improvement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bioptic telescopic lens users file the Low Vision Acuity Screening, form four hundred twelve-LV, with the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit every year, so their screening is an annual filing.

question.text: Where can your vision be tested?

answer.text: Vision can be tested at a branch with an orthorater, a device that checks how well you read at a distance, or by a licensed eye care professional.

teaching.text: A branch can test your vision with an orthorater, which checks distance reading, or a licensed eye care professional can test you instead. Remember: Branch machine or eye doctor.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vision can be tested at a branch with an orthorater, a device that checks how well you read at a distance, or by a licensed eye care professional.

question.text: When must a licensed eye care professional test your vision?

answer.text: A licensed eye care professional must test you if you fail the SCDMV vision test or choose not to be tested at the branch.

teaching.text: Fail the branch vision test, or choose to skip it, and a licensed eye care professional must do the testing. Remember: Fail or skip, see a pro.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A licensed eye care professional must test you if you fail the SCDMV vision test or choose not to be tested at the branch.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Fail or skip, see a pro

question.text: Is the branch vision test required, or may you go straight to an eye care professional?

answer.text: Branch testing is optional: you may skip it and go straight to a licensed eye care professional, who must also test you if you fail the branch test.

teaching.text: The branch test is your choice; going straight to an eye care professional is allowed, and it becomes required after a failed branch test. Remember: Branch test is optional.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Branch testing is optional: you may skip it and go straight to a licensed eye care professional, who must also test you if you fail the branch test.

question.text: How do in-state and out-of-state eye professionals submit vision certificates?

answer.text: SC-licensed eye care professionals submit the Certificate of Vision Examination online, while out-of-state professionals complete SCDMV Form four hundred twelve-NC.

teaching.text: Eye professionals licensed in South Carolina send the vision certificate online, while those licensed elsewhere use SCDMV Form four-twelve-NC. Remember: Online here, form elsewhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: SC-licensed eye care professionals submit the Certificate of Vision Examination online, while out-of-state professionals complete SCDMV Form four hundred twelve-NC.

question.text: How does certificate filing differ for in-state and out-of-state eye professionals?

answer.text: An SC-licensed eye care professional files the vision certificate electronically, while an out-of-state professional fills in Form four hundred twelve-NC on paper.

teaching.text: Where the eye professional is licensed decides the route: in-state means electronic filing, out-of-state means the paper form. Remember: Electronic versus paper.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An SC-licensed eye care professional files the vision certificate electronically, while an out-of-state professional fills in Form four hundred twelve-NC on paper.

question.text: When is vision screening required?

answer.text: Vision screening is required for a first SC permit or license, to remove corrective lens restriction code A, for renewals of a license or permit since October one, two thousand twenty, and when surrendering an out-of-state license.

teaching.text: Vision screening is required for a first permit or license, to remove restriction code A, at each renewal and when you surrender an out-of-state license. Remember: First, restriction, renewal, surrender.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vision screening is required for a first SC permit or license, to remove corrective lens restriction code A, for renewals of a license or permit since October one, two thousand twenty, and when surrendering an out-of-state license.

question.text: How long do standard vision screening certificates stay valid?

answer.text: From May eighteen, two thousand twenty-four, standard vision screening certificates stay valid for thirty-six months.

teaching.text: Since May eighteenth, two thousand twenty-four, a standard vision screening certificate stays good for thirty-six months. Remember: Thirty-six months valid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From May eighteen, two thousand twenty-four, standard vision screening certificates stay valid for thirty-six months.

question.text: What is the minimum vision standard?

answer.text: The minimum vision standard is no stricter than twenty over forty corrected in one eye.

teaching.text: To drive, you must meet a vision standard of twenty forty in at least one eye, with glasses or contacts allowed. Remember: Twenty forty in one eye.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The minimum vision standard is no stricter than twenty over forty corrected in one eye.

question.text: What happens if you meet the vision standard only with glasses or contacts?

answer.text: If you meet the standard only with glasses or contacts, a restriction is added to your permit or license, and driving without those lenses is unlawful.

teaching.text: If you need glasses or contacts to meet the standard, your license carries a restriction, and driving without them breaks the law. Remember: Lenses required, restriction added.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you meet the standard only with glasses or contacts, a restriction is added to your permit or license, and driving without those lenses is unlawful.

question.text: What is the corrective lens restriction code, and what removes it?

answer.text: Corrective lens restriction code A is added when lenses are needed to meet the minimum standard, and removing it requires a vision screening.

teaching.text: The lens restriction is code A, added when lenses are needed, and only a new vision screening can take it off. Remember: Code A, rescreen to remove.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Corrective lens restriction code A is added when lenses are needed to meet the minimum standard, and removing it requires a vision screening.

question.text: How do you remove the lens restriction if your vision improves?

answer.text: If your vision improves so lenses are no longer needed, you provide a new vision certificate from a licensed eye care professional and renew the license to remove the restriction.

teaching.text: When improved vision means you no longer need lenses, bring a new certificate from a licensed eye care professional and renew to drop the restriction. Remember: New certificate, then renew.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your vision improves so lenses are no longer needed, you provide a new vision certificate from a licensed eye care professional and renew the license to remove the restriction.

question.text: What is fatigue, and how does it affect driving?

answer.text: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness from strain, repetitive tasks, illness or lack of sleep, and it can affect vision and slow decisions.

teaching.text: Fatigue is tiredness of body or mind, from strain, repetitive tasks, illness or too little sleep, and it dulls vision and slows decisions. Remember: Tired eyes, slow choices.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness from strain, repetitive tasks, illness or lack of sleep, and it can affect vision and slow decisions.

question.text: How much sleep do most people need to stay alert?

answer.text: Most people need seven to nine hours of sleep a day to stay properly alert during waking hours.

teaching.text: Most people need seven to nine hours of sleep each day to stay properly alert while awake. Remember: Seven to nine nightly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most people need seven to nine hours of sleep a day to stay properly alert during waking hours.

question.text: How often should you plan to stop on a long trip?

answer.text: On long trips, plan to stop about every one hundred miles or two hours.

teaching.text: On long drives, plan a break about every hundred miles or every two hours. Remember: Hundred miles or two hours.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On long trips, plan to stop about every one hundred miles or two hours.

question.text: What other tips help on long trips?

answer.text: Other trip tips are bringing a companion to watch your driving, checking medicine labels for drowsiness warnings and avoiding alcohol and other drugs before or while driving.

teaching.text: Bring a companion, read medicine labels for drowsiness warnings, and skip alcohol and other drugs before and during the trip. Remember: Companion, labels, no alcohol.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other trip tips are bringing a companion to watch your driving, checking medicine labels for drowsiness warnings and avoiding alcohol and other drugs before or while driving.

question.text: What should you do if you begin to feel tired while driving?

answer.text: If you begin to feel tired, pull off at the next exit or rest area and nap for fifteen to twenty minutes, or stop somewhere to sleep for the night.

teaching.text: Once tiredness sets in, get off at the next exit or rest area and nap fifteen to twenty minutes, or stop for the night. Remember: Pull off and nap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you begin to feel tired, pull off at the next exit or rest area and nap for fifteen to twenty minutes, or stop somewhere to sleep for the night.

question.text: What is the best defense against fatigue?

answer.text: Try not to drive late at night, and remember that plenty of rest is the best defense against fatigue.

teaching.text: Avoid late-night driving when you can, and rely on plenty of rest as your best defense against fatigue. Remember: Rest beats fatigue.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Try not to drive late at night, and remember that plenty of rest is the best defense against fatigue.

question.text: What is a distraction, and how dangerous are mental distractions?

answer.text: A distraction is anything that pulls your attention from driving, and mental distractions are as dangerous as taking your eyes off the road or hands off the wheel.

teaching.text: Anything that takes your attention off driving is a distraction, and a distracted mind is as dangerous as wandering eyes or hands. Remember: Mind off road is dangerous.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A distraction is anything that pulls your attention from driving, and mental distractions are as dangerous as taking your eyes off the road or hands off the wheel.

question.text: What phone use is unlawful while driving in South Carolina?

answer.text: In SC it is unlawful to use a wireless electronic communication device while driving if it requires either hand, under SC Code §fifty-six-five-three thousand eight hundred ninety.

teaching.text: South Carolina makes it unlawful to use a wireless communication device while driving when using it takes either hand. Remember: Hands off the phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In SC it is unlawful to use a wireless electronic communication device while driving if it requires either hand, under SC Code §fifty-six-five-three thousand eight hundred ninety.

question.text: Does the South Carolina phone law ban every phone use while driving?

answer.text: The SC phone law targets devices that need the use of either hand while driving, rather than every possible phone use.

teaching.text: The phone law draws its line at hand use; it targets devices that need either hand, not every possible phone use. Remember: Hand use is the line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The SC phone law targets devices that need the use of either hand while driving, rather than every possible phone use.

question.text: Which in-car distractions should you avoid while driving?

answer.text: While driving, avoid arguments and emotional conversations with passengers, avoid eating, make sure children are buckled properly and keep pets in a carrier or portable kennel.

teaching.text: Keep the car calm: skip arguments and emotional talks, do not eat at the wheel, buckle children properly and keep pets in a carrier or kennel. Remember: Calm talk, no snacks, secure pets.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While driving, avoid arguments and emotional conversations with passengers, avoid eating, make sure children are buckled properly and keep pets in a carrier or portable kennel.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Calm talk, no snacks, secure pets

question.text: Who is responsible when distracted driving causes a collision?

answer.text: Distracted driving can cause collisions with injury, death or property damage, and the driver remains responsible for operating the vehicle safely.

teaching.text: When distraction leads to a crash with injury, death or damage, the driver is still the one responsible for safe operation. Remember: Driver stays responsible.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Distracted driving can cause collisions with injury, death or property damage, and the driver remains responsible for operating the vehicle safely.

question.text: How does the manual define aggressive driving?

answer.text: Aggressive driving is an intentional act by a driver that endangers other people or property.

teaching.text: Aggressive driving is a deliberate act by a driver that puts other people or property in danger. Remember: Intentional danger to others.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Aggressive driving is an intentional act by a driver that endangers other people or property.

question.text: Which behaviors are typical of aggressive driving?

answer.text: Typical aggressive driving behaviors are speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, signaling improperly or not at all, and ignoring traffic control devices.

teaching.text: Speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, poor or missing signals and ignoring traffic control devices are the typical aggressive behaviors. Remember: Speed, tailgate, weave, ignore.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Typical aggressive driving behaviors are speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, signaling improperly or not at all, and ignoring traffic control devices.

question.text: Is failing to obey stop signs or signals considered aggressive driving?

answer.text: Speeding and tailgating are listed as aggressive behaviors, and so is failing to obey stop signs, yield signs, traffic signals or railroad crossing signals.

teaching.text: Running stop signs, yield signs, traffic signals or railroad crossing signals is aggressive driving too, not just speeding and tailgating. Remember: Ignoring signals is aggressive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding and tailgating are listed as aggressive behaviors, and so is failing to obey stop signs, yield signs, traffic signals or railroad crossing signals.

question.text: What share of fatal traffic collisions involve alcohol and other impairing drugs?

answer.text: Alcohol and other impairing drugs are involved in about forty percent of traffic collisions that kill someone each year.

teaching.text: About forty percent of the traffic collisions that kill someone each year involve alcohol or other impairing drugs. Remember: Alcohol in many fatal crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol and other impairing drugs are involved in about forty percent of traffic collisions that kill someone each year.

question.text: What alcohol rules apply to drivers under twenty-one?

answer.text: Drivers under twenty-one may not legally buy, possess or drink alcohol, and every state has zero tolerance or similar laws for drivers under twenty-one.

teaching.text: Under twenty-one, buying, possessing or drinking alcohol is illegal, and every state has zero tolerance or similar laws for young drivers. Remember: Under twenty-one, zero tolerance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers under twenty-one may not legally buy, possess or drink alcohol, and every state has zero tolerance or similar laws for drivers under twenty-one.

question.text: Why do alcohol and drugs affect new drivers more?

answer.text: Alcohol and impairing drugs hit new drivers harder because they are still learning complex skills.

teaching.text: Because new drivers are still learning complex skills, alcohol and impairing drugs affect them even more. Remember: Learners hit harder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs hit new drivers harder because they are still learning complex skills.

question.text: How do alcohol and impairing drugs affect judgment?

answer.text: Alcohol and other impairing drugs reduce judgment, the brain's quick use of stored experience and knowledge when facing a new problem.

teaching.text: Alcohol and impairing drugs weaken judgment, the brain's quick use of experience and knowledge to solve a new problem. Remember: Judgment goes first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol and other impairing drugs reduce judgment, the brain's quick use of stored experience and knowledge when facing a new problem.

question.text: How does alcohol affect vision and distance judgment?

answer.text: Alcohol blurs vision, slows focusing, can cause double vision and weakens your judgment of distance, speed and other vehicles' movement, with vision affected at zero point zero two percent BAC for every driver.

teaching.text: Alcohol blurs and slows your vision, may cause double vision and throws off your sense of distance and speed, starting at point zero two percent BAC. Remember: Blurred eyes, bad distances.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol blurs vision, slows focusing, can cause double vision and weakens your judgment of distance, speed and other vehicles' movement, with vision affected at zero point zero two percent BAC for every driver.

question.text: What else does alcohol reduce besides vision?

answer.text: Alcohol also reduces your ability to tell colors apart and slows your reaction time.

teaching.text: Alcohol also makes colors harder to tell apart and slows how fast you react. Remember: Colors fade, reactions slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol also reduces your ability to tell colors apart and slows your reaction time.

question.text: When does alcohol impairment begin?

answer.text: Impairment begins with the first drink, and anyone with even one drink in the bloodstream could be arrested for driving under the influence.

teaching.text: Impairment starts with the very first drink, and even one drink in your bloodstream could lead to an arrest for driving under the influence. Remember: First drink, impairment starts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Impairment begins with the first drink, and anyone with even one drink in the bloodstream could be arrested for driving under the influence.

question.text: What does BAC mean?

answer.text: BAC, blood alcohol concentration, is the percentage of alcohol relative to the amount of blood in your body.

teaching.text: BAC, or blood alcohol concentration, measures alcohol as a percentage of the blood in your body. Remember: Alcohol share of blood.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: BAC, blood alcohol concentration, is the percentage of alcohol relative to the amount of blood in your body.

question.text: What is the manual's best advice about drinking and driving?

answer.text: The manual's best advice is not to drive any vehicle after drinking alcohol or using other drugs, and never to let a friend or relative drive after drinking.

teaching.text: The manual's best advice is simple: do not drive after drinking or using drugs, and never let a friend or relative drive after drinking. Remember: Drink, then do not drive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual's best advice is not to drive any vehicle after drinking alcohol or using other drugs, and never to let a friend or relative drive after drinking.

question.text: Can anyone drink alcohol or use impairing drugs and still drive safely?

answer.text: The manual says no one can drink alcohol or use other impairing drugs and still drive safely.

teaching.text: The manual is clear that no one can drink alcohol or use impairing drugs and still drive safely. Remember: No one drinks safely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual says no one can drink alcohol or use other impairing drugs and still drive safely.

question.text: Which events may lead to suspension of your license and driving privileges?

answer.text: A DUI or DUAC conviction, a BAC of zero point one five percent or more, or refusing implied consent testing may lead to suspension of your license and driving privileges.

teaching.text: A DUI or DUAC conviction, a BAC of point one five percent or more, or refusing implied consent testing can each lead to suspension. Remember: Conviction, high BAC, refusal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A DUI or DUAC conviction, a BAC of zero point one five percent or more, or refusing implied consent testing may lead to suspension of your license and driving privileges.

question.text: Can you be convicted of impaired driving below the higher BAC levels?

answer.text: You can be convicted of impaired driving with a BAC of only zero point zero five, or lower when combined with drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

teaching.text: A conviction for impaired driving is possible at a BAC of only point zero five, or even lower when drugs, including medicines, are involved. Remember: Low BAC can convict.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You can be convicted of impaired driving with a BAC of only zero point zero five, or lower when combined with drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

question.text: What do the three BAC levels in the manual each signal?

answer.text: A BAC of zero point one five percent or more is a suspension trigger, a BAC of zero point zero five can still support an impaired-driving conviction, and zero point zero two is where vision is already affected.

teaching.text: Keep the three alcohol numbers apart: point one five triggers suspension, point zero five can support a conviction, and point zero two already affects vision. Remember: Fifteen, five, two hundredths.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A BAC of zero point one five percent or more is a suspension trigger, a BAC of zero point zero five can still support an impaired-driving conviction, and zero point zero two is where vision is already affected.

question.text: What happens to a driver under twenty-one who registers a BAC of point zero two or more?

answer.text: A driver under twenty-one who registers a BAC of zero point zero two percent or more has the privilege to drive suspended immediately for at least three months.

teaching.text: For a driver under twenty-one, a reading of point zero two percent or more suspends the privilege to drive right away, for at least three months. Remember: Two hundredths, three months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver under twenty-one who registers a BAC of zero point zero two percent or more has the privilege to drive suspended immediately for at least three months.

question.text: What happens to a driver under twenty-one who refuses an intoxicant test?

answer.text: A driver under twenty-one who refuses the test for intoxicants immediately loses driving privileges for at least six months.

teaching.text: A driver under twenty-one who refuses the intoxicant test loses driving privileges immediately, for at least six months. Remember: Refuse, six months gone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver under twenty-one who refuses the test for intoxicants immediately loses driving privileges for at least six months.

question.text: What does South Carolina's implied consent law mean for a licensed driver?

answer.text: Under SC's implied consent law, getting a license means you have agreed in advance to a lawful breath, blood or urine test if suspected of impaired driving, and refusing can cost you your license.

teaching.text: With a South Carolina license, you have already agreed to a lawful breath, blood or urine test if suspected of impaired driving, and refusal can cost the license. Remember: License means consent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under SC's implied consent law, getting a license means you have agreed in advance to a lawful breath, blood or urine test if suspected of impaired driving, and refusing can cost you your license.

question.text: Which tests may be used under implied consent?

answer.text: An alcohol concentration test is usually done by breath, blood or urine, and a police officer may require all three under implied consent.

teaching.text: Implied consent testing usually means breath, blood or urine, and an officer may require all three. Remember: Breath, blood, urine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An alcohol concentration test is usually done by breath, blood or urine, and a police officer may require all three under implied consent.

question.text: Whose implied consent law applies if you are arrested in another state?

answer.text: Implied consent laws differ by state, and the law of the state where you are arrested applies, not the state that issued your license.

teaching.text: Each state has its own implied consent law, and the one that applies is the law of the state where you are arrested. Remember: Arrest state rules.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Implied consent laws differ by state, and the law of the state where you are arrested applies, not the state that issued your license.

question.text: Can prescription and over-the-counter drugs affect driving like alcohol?

answer.text: Many prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect driving as much as alcohol or worse.

teaching.text: Plenty of prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving as much as alcohol, or even more. Remember: Pills can impair too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect driving as much as alcohol or worse.

question.text: What effects can common medicines and pep pills have on drivers?

answer.text: Over-the-counter medicines for headaches, colds, allergies or nerves can cause drowsiness, while pep pills, uppers and diet pills can cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration and vision problems.

teaching.text: Medicines for headaches, colds, allergies or nerves can make you drowsy, and pep pills, uppers or diet pills can cause nervousness, dizziness and vision trouble. Remember: Drowsy or jittery.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Over-the-counter medicines for headaches, colds, allergies or nerves can cause drowsiness, while pep pills, uppers and diet pills can cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration and vision problems.

question.text: What should you do before taking any medicine and driving?

answer.text: Check the label of any medicine for warnings before taking it, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

teaching.text: Before taking a medicine, read its label for warnings, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving. Remember: Read the label first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check the label of any medicine for warnings before taking it, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

question.text: How is a drug DUI conviction treated in South Carolina?

answer.text: A conviction in SC for driving under the influence of drugs is treated the same as a DUI or DUAC conviction.

teaching.text: In South Carolina, a conviction for driving under the influence of drugs counts the same as a DUI or DUAC conviction. Remember: Drug DUI equals DUI.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A conviction in SC for driving under the influence of drugs is treated the same as a DUI or DUAC conviction.

question.text: Why should you never drink alcohol while taking other drugs?

answer.text: Never drink alcohol while taking other drugs, because they can multiply alcohol's effects or add effects of their own.

teaching.text: Never combine alcohol with other drugs, because they can multiply alcohol's effects or bring new effects of their own. Remember: Mixing multiplies effects.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never drink alcohol while taking other drugs, because they can multiply alcohol's effects or add effects of their own.

question.text: Can legal prescription drugs affect driving the way illegal drugs can?

answer.text: Prescription and illegal drugs can both affect reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness in ways similar to alcohol.

teaching.text: Prescription drugs and illegal drugs can both dull reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness much like alcohol does. Remember: Legal or not, impairing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Prescription and illegal drugs can both affect reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness in ways similar to alcohol.

question.text: What should you do if strong emotions affect you before driving?

answer.text: Strong emotions interfere with thinking, attention and processing information, so if you are angry or worried, cool off first, perhaps with a short walk or nap, or let someone else drive.

teaching.text: Strong emotions crowd out clear thinking, so if you are angry or worried, cool off with a short walk or nap, or let someone else drive. Remember: Cool off first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Strong emotions interfere with thinking, attention and processing information, so if you are angry or worried, cool off first, perhaps with a short walk or nap, or let someone else drive.

question.text: Which emotions can keep you from driving well?

answer.text: Extreme levels of any emotion, not only anger, can keep you from driving well, and staying off the road until symptoms pass is the safest choice.

teaching.text: Any emotion at an extreme level, not just anger, can make you a poor driver, so wait until it passes. Remember: Any extreme emotion.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Extreme levels of any emotion, not only anger, can keep you from driving well, and staying off the road until symptoms pass is the safest choice.

question.text: How can aging affect a driver?

answer.text: Aging can dull hearing and eyesight, slow judgment and reaction in emergencies, and leave an older driver unaware of new rules and regulations.

teaching.text: Getting older can dull hearing and eyesight, slow judgment and emergency reactions, and leave a driver out of date on new rules. Remember: Age dulls senses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Aging can dull hearing and eyesight, slow judgment and reaction in emergencies, and leave an older driver unaware of new rules and regulations.

question.text: Why may older drivers react more slowly in an emergency?

answer.text: Older drivers may not have the same ability to act quickly in an emergency as before, because physical dexterity may weaken with age.

teaching.text: Older drivers may react less quickly in an emergency because physical dexterity can weaken with age. Remember: Dexterity may weaken.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Older drivers may not have the same ability to act quickly in an emergency as before, because physical dexterity may weaken with age.

question.text: What should happen if several warning signs apply to an older driver?

answer.text: If two or three of the listed warning signs apply to an older driver, it may be time to change driving habits or stop driving, and a doctor may refer the driver for an assessment by an SCDMV examiner or another trained medical professional.

teaching.text: When two or three warning signs fit an older driver, it may be time to change habits or stop, and a doctor may refer an assessment. Remember: Signs mean reassess.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If two or three of the listed warning signs apply to an older driver, it may be time to change driving habits or stop driving, and a doctor may refer the driver for an assessment by an SCDMV examiner or another trained medical professional.
